meta.title: How much does custom software cost in Quebec? (2026 prices)
meta.description: Real published prices: sprints from $4,500, management software from $12,000 to $30,000 in phases. What drives cost, timelines, ESSOR, pitfalls.
meta.ogTitle: How much does custom software cost in Quebec — real 2026 prices

coutLogiciel.title: How much does custom software cost in Quebec?
coutLogiciel.byline: By <author>Gabriel Nadon</author>, business software developer for SMBs
coutLogiciel.summary: With me, a first fixed-scope sprint costs from $4,500 and is delivered in 2 to 3 weeks. A complete management system is then built in phases of about $6,000; most end up at $12,000 to $30,000 in total. The price depends mainly on the number of screens and business rules, the data to bring over (Excel, Access) and the software to connect. Also plan for maintenance after delivery.

sections.h: How much does custom software cost for an SMB?
p: The price of custom software depends less on the technology than on the scope: how many screens, how many business rules, how much data to bring over and how many systems to connect. Here are my prices, published as is so you can compare the quotes you receive.

table.caption: Custom software prices by scope (Gabriel Nadon’s prices, 2026)
head: Scope
Concrete example
Price
Timeline
rows: Import supplier price lists, produce quotes from a template
Work orders and timesheets connected to payroll
Quotes, projects, hours, inventory and invoicing in one place
Multiple sites, client portal, many integrations

after: The first row matters most: you start with the task that costs you the most today, at a fixed scope and price. If it doesn’t pay off, you haven’t committed $30,000 to find out. That’s how <cas>the grocery store case worth $56,000 a year</cas> started.

sections.h: What do you get for $5,000, $15,000 or $30,000?

table.caption: What a budget gets you (typical examples, Gabriel Nadon’s prices)
head: Budget
What you get
Typical example
rows: One manual task eliminated, connected to your existing tools
Supplier price lists imported and compared automatically
A small management system: two or three modules that talk to each other
Quotes + work orders + hours, with export to your accounting software
The company’s management software, built in roughly five phases
Quotes, projects, inventory, hours, invoicing and a dashboard

after: These are typical examples to help you place a budget, not packages: the actual price is set after the assessment, phase by phase, at a fixed scope.

sections.h: What makes the price go up or down?
list: The number of screens and business rules. A simple data entry form costs little; a quote calculation with discounts, taxes and client-specific exceptions costs more.
The data to bring over. Clean Excel files import quickly. Years of history with duplicates, inconsistent formats and hidden formulas need cleanup — that’s often where projects go off the rails.
The software to connect. QuickBooks, Acomba, Sage, an ERP or an API: each integration adds work, and some software only offers file imports.
Who uses it, and where. Three people at the office, or twenty employees in the field with a phone and different access rights.
Personal information. If the system holds client or employee data, Quebec’s Law 25 requires security measures and an incident register (Quebec’s privacy regulator). Plan for it from the start.

sections.h: Fixed price or hourly rate: how to read a quote
p: An hourly rate puts the risk on the client: if the project goes off the rails, the bill follows. A fixed price with a fixed scope puts the risk on the developer, as long as the scope is clearly written. I work at a fixed price, in phases.
A good quote should include, at a minimum:
list: the list of screens, calculations and reports delivered — what’s included and what isn’t;
the data brought over (which files, how many years of history) and the software connected;
the schedule for each stage and what you’ll be able to use at the end of each one;
ownership: handover of the source code, the documentation and all access;
after delivery: hosting, backups, fixes and what they cost.

sections.h: How long does it take to develop custom software?
p: Count on 2 to 3 weeks for a first task eliminated and running on your real data. A complete management system is built in several phases, each one delivered and used before the next.

“All at once” projects lasting six to eighteen months are the ones that go off the rails most often: the need changes while it’s being built, and nobody uses anything until the end. Working in phases gives you something useful from the first month.

sections.h: Is custom software worth the investment?
p: Do the math before asking for a quote: hours per week × number of people × loaded hourly rate × 50 weeks. One person spending 10 hours a week re-keying data at $35 an hour costs $17,500 a year.

If the targeted task costs less than the project over 12 months, custom software probably isn’t the right choice for it. And if off-the-shelf software does 80% of the job, buy it: custom software makes sense when the way you work is a competitive advantage, or when you’re paying for several subscriptions that don’t talk to each other.

sections.h: Custom software or off-the-shelf software: what’s the difference?
p: Off-the-shelf software is sold to many businesses, and you configure it. Custom software is built around your process, and you own it.

table.caption: Off-the-shelf or custom software
head: Criterion
Off-the-shelf software
Custom software
rows: You adapt your process to the software
The software adapts to your process
The vendor keeps the software and its rules
You receive the code, the data and the access
Fast if the need is standard
In phases, the first in 2 to 3 weeks

sections.h: What grants are available for a software project in Quebec?
p: The <essor>Investissement Québec ESSOR program</essor> (Component 1) is the main option, and it ends on March 31, 2027. Component 1B covers 50% of a digital assessment and plan, up to $20,000; Component 1C covers 50% of implementing that plan, up to $50,000, for a project of 12 months or less. Both target businesses with 250 employees or fewer and annual revenue of at least $2.5M, and 1C requires a plan completed under 1B within the last 24 months.

The trap to avoid: the program guides exclude expenses incurred before the application is filed, including contractual commitments. Don’t sign anything before you’ve applied. The 1C guide doesn’t say whether custom development is eligible: get Investissement Québec to confirm it. As for Revenu Québec’s C3i tax credit, it covers acquired assets (hardware, management software packages), not custom development.

sections.h: What costs should you plan for after delivery?
p: Software is a living thing: hosting, backups, security updates, small fixes and improvements. With me, the system is handed over documented with all its access, and support is agreed on together — per phase or under a monthly agreement. Always ask who will maintain the system three years from now; that’s the question that separates a good price from a low one.

meta.title: Replacing an Access database in 2026: options, cost, migration
meta.description: Access 2016 and 2019 lost support in October 2025, Access 2021 in October 2026. Options compared, costs, timelines and migration without data loss.
meta.ogTitle: Replacing an Access database in 2026 — options compared and migration

remplacerAccess.title: Replacing an Access database in 2026: with what, for how much, and how to migrate
remplacerAccess.byline: By <author>Gabriel Nadon</author>, business software developer for SMBs
remplacerAccess.summary: Access still exists, but Access 2016 and 2019 have not received security updates since October 14, 2025, and Access 2021 since October 14, 2026 (Microsoft). If your database runs on one of these versions, there are three realistic paths: move to a supported version and stabilize the database, move the data to SQL Server while keeping the Access screens, or replace the application with web software. In all three cases, you start by taking stock of what the database really does.

sections.h: Does Access still exist?
p: Yes. It’s the one-time purchase versions that are reaching end of support, one after the other. According to <msft>Microsoft</msft>, after the end date there are no more security updates, no more fixes and no more support, free or paid. The software keeps starting up — which is exactly what makes the risk invisible.

table.caption: End of support for Access versions (Microsoft)
head: Version
End of support
What it means
rows: No more security updates, as of a few days ago
Supported, but with a known end date
Updated as long as the subscription is active

after: On October 14, 2025, Windows 10 also reached end of support. An Access database running on an old Windows 10 computer therefore carries two risks. The dates for <v2021>Access 2021</v2021> and <v2024>Access 2024</v2024> come from Microsoft’s lifecycle pages.

sections.h: When should you replace an Access database?
list: Several people use it at the same time on a network drive, and the database gets corrupted or slows down.
The file keeps growing. An Access file is capped at 2 GB (Microsoft’s official specifications).
You want remote access or access from a phone, at a job site or in a warehouse.
Only one person understands the VBA code, and they’ve left or will be leaving soon.
The database holds personal information (clients, employees) on a computer that no longer gets updates: Quebec’s Law 25 requires reasonable security measures (Quebec’s privacy regulator).

sections.h: What can replace Access?
p: There’s no single replacement: the right choice depends on the number of users, remote access needs and how much business logic is hidden in the macros.

table.caption: Options for replacing an Access database
head: Option
Best for
Advantage
Limitation
rows: Database that works well, few users
Same limits: 2 GB, local network, Windows computer
Data in SQL Server, Access screens kept
The VBA code still needs maintaining
Business already on Microsoft 365, simple needs
Mobile, little code; Microsoft documents how to migrate the tables
Power Apps licence that includes Dataverse; only supported data types migrate
You adapt the way you work
Specific processes, remote access, multiple sites
Built for you, and you own it
Longer project, best done in phases

after: For most SMBs, the second option is a good first step: you secure the data in SQL Server without changing anyone’s habits, then replace the screens with a web application, piece by piece, if the business needs it.

sections.h: How do you migrate an Access database without losing data?
list: Inventory. List the tables, queries, forms, reports, macros and VBA modules, as well as tables linked to other files. That’s where the business rules hide.
Verified backup. Copy the file and test that it can be restored, before touching anything.
Cleanup. Fix duplicates, inconsistent data types and text fields that contain dates.

Data migration. Microsoft provides a free tool, the SQL Server Migration Assistant for Access (SSMA), which moves the tables to SQL Server or Azure SQL and lets you link the existing Access forms to the new tables.
Checks. Compare the totals (row counts, sums, balances) between the old and new databases. They must match.
Cutover. Run both in parallel for a few days, then switch over one evening or weekend.
after: The usual pitfalls: VBA code and macros, which don’t migrate on their own; queries written in Access’s own SQL dialect; AutoNumber, Yes/No, multivalued and Attachment fields, which behave differently; and printed reports, which have to be rebuilt. If you’re aiming for Power Apps, Microsoft notes that <dataverse>only supported data types are exported to Dataverse</dataverse>.

sections.h: How long does it take to replace an Access database?
p: Securing the data in SQL Server while keeping the Access screens usually takes a first sprint of 2 to 3 weeks. Replacing the screens with a web application then happens in phases, one group of forms at a time: your employees keep working in the old database while the new one grows.
What makes a project longer is almost never the number of tables: it’s the logic hidden in the VBA, the reports that must be rebuilt exactly, and the data that needs cleaning.

sections.h: How much does it cost to replace an Access database?
p: The cost depends mainly on the number of forms, reports and lines of VBA code, much more than on the number of tables. With me, a first fixed-scope sprint starts at $4,500 for 2 to 3 weeks — often enough to secure the data in SQL Server. Replacing all the screens is then done in phases of about $6,000. The details are in the custom software pricing guide.

meta.title: Taking over old WinDev or Access software: where to start
meta.description: The developer left and the software runs your business? What to check before touching it, then maintain, modernize or replace, with prices.
meta.ogTitle: Taking over abandoned in-house software — the method, step by step

repriseLogiciel.title: Taking over abandoned WinDev, Access or in-house software: where to start
repriseLogiciel.byline: By <author>Gabriel Nadon</author>, business software developer for SMBs
repriseLogiciel.summary: Before rewriting anything, you secure what’s there: recover the source code and the access, make a complete, verified backup, then document what the software really does. Only then do you choose: keep it as is, stabilize it and modernize it piece by piece, or replace it in stages. A complete rewrite all at once is rarely the right first decision.

sections.h: The 7 checks before touching anything
list: The source code, not just the installed program. Without it, you can only work around problems, never fix them.
The development tools and licences. WinDev, for example, is a commercial environment from PC SOFT: changing the code requires a licence from the vendor.
The access: server, database, hosting, domain name, administrator accounts. They’re often in the former developer’s name.
A backup that has been successfully restored. A backup that has never been tested isn’t a backup.
The dependencies: Windows version, printer or barcode scanner drivers, libraries, database (HFSQL for WinDev, .accdb file for Access).
Who uses what, and the tasks that can only be done in this software.
What breaks most often, and what the team already does to work around it.

sections.h: The developer left and you don’t have the source code: what now?
p: It’s the most common situation, and it’s almost never hopeless. Start by looking for the code: the former supplier’s contract or invoice, the former developer’s computer, the server, backups, a USB key forgotten in a drawer. For a WinDev project, you need the project files, not just the installed program (.exe).

If the code can’t be found, the data can almost always be recovered: an HFSQL database or an Access file can be read and exported without the program. The application can then be rebuilt around the existing data, in stages, by observing what the old software does screen by screen.
To keep it from happening again: require every supplier, in writing, to hand over the source code, the documentation and all access, in your company’s name.

sections.h: How do you find a developer to take over software?
p: Look for someone who offers to read the software first, not rebuild it. Three questions quickly separate the candidates: have they already taken over software written by someone else in that language? Do they start with an inventory and a backup? What do they hand over at the end — code, documentation, access?
Be wary of “it all needs to be redone” before they’ve even seen the code. Sometimes it’s true, but that gets shown after the inventory, not before.

sections.h: What’s the future of WinDev, Access and old Windows software?
p: WinDev is still sold by PC SOFT, and Access is still offered by Microsoft. The real question isn’t the tool’s future, but your software’s: who can fix it when it crashes, and what computer it runs on. Since October 14, 2025, Windows 10, Access 2016 and Access 2019 no longer receive security updates (<msft>Microsoft</msft>). In-house software that depends on any of them becomes a risk, even if it still works.

sections.h: Maintain, modernize or replace?

table.caption: The three paths after a takeover
head: Path
When to choose it
Risk
Price range
rows: The software does its job well, few changes planned
Low in the short term, the dependency remains
Stabilize, then modernize piece by piece
The software is critical but fragile; you want to keep existing habits
Low: you change one part at a time
Sprint from $4,500, then phases of about $6,000
The software is holding back growth or can no longer be changed
Medium: the data migration must be checked

sections.h: What software should replace WinDev or Access?
p: There’s no single best language: choose a widely used technology that other developers will be able to take over after you. For an SMB, that’s often a web application (PHP/Laravel, .NET or Python) with a standard SQL database, accessible from any computer or phone. If your needs are standard, off-the-shelf software may be enough.

The data from the old system (HFSQL, Access) is migrated to the new database; you check that the totals match before switching over. For Access, the method is detailed in <access>the guide to replacing an Access database</access>.

sections.h: How much does it cost to take over software?
p: The 20-minute assessment is free. The takeover starts with a fixed-scope, fixed-price sprint, from $4,500: inventory, verified backup, fixes for blocking bugs and documentation. The rest is done in phases of about $6,000, at the pace of your operations. Pricing details are in the custom software pricing guide, and the service is described on the legacy software takeover page.

meta.title: Replacing Excel with business software: options and prices
meta.description: When Excel isn’t enough: what to choose (online tool, off-the-shelf or custom software), what it costs and how to migrate without losing your formulas.
meta.ogTitle: Replacing Excel with business software — options compared and real prices

remplacerExcel.title: Replacing Excel with business software: when, with what, and for how much
remplacerExcel.byline: By <author>Gabriel Nadon</author>, business software developer for SMBs
remplacerExcel.summary: Excel becomes a problem when several people edit the same file, when data gets re-keyed elsewhere, or when only one person understands the formulas. There are three families of replacements: an online tool (Airtable, Smartsheet, Power Apps), off-the-shelf software (accounting, ERP) or custom software. Custom software makes sense when your process is specific; with me, you start with a single task, from $4,500 in 2 to 3 weeks.

sections.h: What are the signs that Excel isn’t enough anymore?
list: Several versions of the same file are circulating and nobody knows which one is right.
The same data gets re-keyed in Excel, then in the accounting software, then in an email.
Only one person understands the formulas or macros, and everything stops when they’re away.
Field teams can’t use it properly on a phone, at a job site or in a warehouse.
A formula error has already been costly: an underpriced quote, wrong inventory, a payroll to correct.
The file holds personal information (clients, employees) that everyone can access: Quebec’s Law 25 requires reasonable security measures (Quebec’s privacy regulator).
Your version of Excel is no longer supported: Excel 2016 and 2019 have not received security updates since October 14, 2025 (Microsoft).

sections.h: What can replace Excel?
p: There’s no single right replacement: it all depends on how much of your process is standard, and how much is unique to you.

table.caption: The three families of Excel replacements
head: Option
Examples
Best for
Limitation
rows: Teams that want to share simple lists and tracking
Per-user subscription; complex logic quickly becomes fragile
You adapt the way you work to the software
Quotes, work orders, hours, inventory based on your rules
Specific processes, several tools that don’t talk to each other
Project to break into phases; you need a developer who sticks around

after: A hybrid approach is often best: you keep your accounting software, and the custom software only covers what it doesn’t do, by connecting to it.

sections.h: When is custom software worth it?
list: The way you calculate a quote, plan work or track production is an advantage, and no off-the-shelf software can reproduce it.
You pay for three or four subscriptions that each cover part of the need, and someone copies data from one to the other.
The task to replace costs more per year than the project: hours per week × people × hourly rate × 50 weeks.
If off-the-shelf software does 80% of the job, buy it — I’ll tell you so during the assessment.

sections.h: How do you migrate an Excel file without losing its formulas?
list: Inventory. List the sheets, formulas, macros and links to other files. The formulas are your business rules: they get written down in black and white.
Cleanup. Duplicates, merged cells, dates entered as text, inconsistent product codes.
Rebuilding the rules. Each calculation becomes a rule tested in the software, with real examples.
Import. The useful data and history are imported; the rest is archived.
Checks. The totals in the software and in Excel must match for the same period.
Parallel run. A few days with both, then the file is closed.

sections.h: How much does it cost to replace Excel, and how long does it take?
p: With me, the first task replaced costs from $4,500 and is delivered in 2 to 3 weeks, at a fixed scope. A complete management system is then built in phases of about $6,000; most end up at $12,000 to $30,000 in total. The details are in the custom software pricing guide.

A real example: an independent grocery store in Quebec received its suppliers’ price lists in Excel, CSV and PDF, and re-keyed them into its point-of-sale system — nearly $56,000 a year in staff time. The system now imports and compares them automatically, connected to the existing point-of-sale system. <cas>Read the full case</cas>.

meta.title: Custom software maintenance: what it costs and what to require
meta.description: What custom software maintenance costs per year, what it covers, what a contract should include and what to do if the developer disappears.
meta.ogTitle: Custom software maintenance — the real yearly cost and the pitfalls

maintenanceLogiciel.title: Custom software maintenance: how much per year, and what to require
maintenanceLogiciel.byline: By <author>Gabriel Nadon</author>, business software developer for SMBs
maintenanceLogiciel.summary: Plan a yearly maintenance budget: Witify, a Quebec firm, recommends 10% to 15% of the initial cost per year, or $2,000 to $3,000 a year for a $20,000 system. That budget covers hosting, backups, security updates, fixes and small improvements. Before signing, require the source code, the documentation and the access in your company’s name: that’s what protects you if the supplier disappears.

sections.h: What does custom software maintenance cover?
list: Fixes: a calculation that’s wrong, a screen that crashes, a report that no longer runs.
Security: updates to libraries, the server and certificates. Software that’s never updated becomes vulnerable, even if it still works.
Backups: automatic, and above all tested with an actual restore.
Hosting: server or cloud, domain name, emails sent by the system.
Compatibility: new versions of Windows, browsers and the connected accounting software. A recent example: Windows 10 has not been supported since October 14, 2025 (Microsoft).
Small improvements: one more field, a new report, a rule that changes.

sections.h: How much does maintenance cost per year?
p: The rule published by Witify, a Quebec firm, is 10% to 15% of the initial cost per year. For a $20,000 system, that means $2,000 to $3,000 a year, plus hosting depending on usage.
With me, support is agreed on together after delivery — per phase, or under a monthly agreement — and the system is handed over documented, with all its access. You’re never locked in.

sections.h: What should a maintenance contract specify?
list: the response time for a blocking outage, and for an ordinary request;
what’s included (fixes, security updates, backups) and what’s billed separately (improvements);
how often backups run and how restores are tested;
the price of improvements: fixed price per request or a bank of hours;
reversibility: handover of the code, the documentation and the access if you change suppliers.

sections.h: What happens if the developer disappears?
p: Without the source code and the access, every fix becomes a workaround. With them, another developer can take over the software. Be careful: in Canada, the author of software is the first owner of its copyright, and an assignment is only valid if it’s in writing and signed (<lda>Copyright Act, s. 13</lda>). An outside supplier therefore doesn’t transfer the code to you by default: put it in the contract.
If it has already happened, the method is in <reprise>the guide to taking over old software</reprise>.

sections.h: Maintenance is part of your obligations under Quebec’s Law 25
p: If your software holds personal information (clients, employees), you must take reasonable security measures and keep a register of confidentiality incidents (<cai>Quebec’s privacy regulator</cai>). Software that’s never updated, with no tested backup, is hard to defend after an incident.

Published rates in Quebec range from about $25 to $80/h for an offshore team, $80 to $160/h for a senior developer in Canada and $125 to $250/h for a local agency (Witify, 2026). In every case, require a price per stage, the source code and the access in your name.

sections.h: Questions to ask before signing

Payment per stage, tied to usable deliverables.
Assignment of the copyright in the code, in writing and signed: without it, the outside developer remains the owner (Copyright Act, s. 13).
The access: hosting, database, domain name and accounts in your company’s name.
Personal information: who has access to it and how it’s protected (Quebec’s Law 25).
After delivery: maintenance, response times, price of improvements — see the maintenance guide.

subventionsLogiciel.title: Grants for a software project in Quebec: what’s really eligible
subventionsLogiciel.byline: By <author>Gabriel Nadon</author>, business software developer for SMBs
subventionsLogiciel.summary: The main program is Investissement Québec’s ESSOR program (Component 1): 50% of a digital assessment and plan, up to $20,000 (1B), then 50% of implementation, up to $50,000 (1C), for businesses with 250 employees or fewer and at least $2.5M in revenue, until March 31, 2027. Golden rule: don’t sign anything before the application is filed. The C3i credit covers purchased assets, not custom development.

after: The ESSOR program ends on March 31, 2027, and Investissement Québec can suspend applications without notice: check the status on the official page before building your budget.

sections.h: The trap that cancels the grant: spending before applying
p: The ESSOR 1B and 1C guides exclude expenses incurred before the application is filed, including contractual commitments. Signing a quote or paying a deposit before applying can make those expenses ineligible. Also excluded: internal expenses, capital assets and taxes.
The order to follow: get the quotes, file the application, wait for the answer, then sign.

sections.h: Is custom development eligible?
p: The 1B guide covers the assessment, the digital plan and system selection. The 1C guide funds implementing the plan, but doesn’t say explicitly whether developing custom software is eligible. Get Investissement Québec to confirm it, in writing, before you commit.
For a small project (under $30,000), the most realistic route is often to start with a 1B assessment, which documents the need and sets up what comes next.

sections.h: How to prepare an application for a software project
list: Describe the problem in numbers: hours lost per week, errors, yearly cost.
Get a quote broken into stages, with scope, schedule and deliverables.
File the 1B application (assessment) before any commitment; then the 1C, within 24 months.
Keep invoices and proof of payment, and stay within the 12-month maximum project length for 1C.
